title: Renaming an environment silently breaks script environment pins and folder overrides — presets then run against whatever environment is active
existing_state: EnvironmentService.RenameEnvironment (Services/EnvironmentService.cs:216-255) re-keys the map and follows the active/base pointers, but nothing cascades to the two other places environment names are stored: YAML scripts' `environment:` headers (preset content) and per-folder FolderInfo.BaseEnvironment overrides (Models/FolderInfo.cs:12). After a rename, loading a preset that declares the old name hits the missing-environment branch in ApplyPresetEnvironmentOnPresetLoad (Form1.cs:2186-2192): a status-bar message is shown, the auto-switch is skipped, and the preset remains loaded against the CURRENTLY ACTIVE environment's host grid. In a multi-host fleet tool this means a script pinned to e.g. "staging" can be executed against the production host list with only a transient status-bar hint, and folder base-environment overrides dangle silently.
recommendation: On rename, cascade: update FolderInfo.BaseEnvironment entries matching the old name (Services/PresetManager folders via the same config Update), and scan preset Commands for a YAML `environment:` header equal to the old name, offering a one-click rewrite (the parser already exposes TryGetScriptDeclaredEnvironment, Form1.cs:2201+). Independently, harden the failure mode: when a preset's declared environment is missing, raise a modal/blocking confirmation before run rather than a status-bar note.
user_benefit: Eliminates a wrong-target hazard: renaming an environment can currently cause environment-pinned scripts to run against the wrong host fleet with effectively no warning.

evidence.note: rename updates only the map + active/base pointers
folder BaseEnvironment override stores the name, never rewritten
missing environment -> status-bar message only; preset stays loaded on active environment
